designSystem.name: Brain Assistant Dark Technical

principles: Use visual hierarchy rather than decorative elements
Use teal as the single primary accent color
Keep surfaces visually distinct but close in tone
Use consistent spacing based on a 4px grid
Keep navigation visually stable across screens
Avoid visual clichés associated with AI products

rules: Use 8px radius for normal cards and controls
Use 12px radius only for large containers or dialogs
Circular shapes are reserved for avatars and floating action buttons
Avoid excessive pill-shaped controls except tags and statuses
Normal cards should not use visible drop shadows
Use shadows only for floating elements
Prefer surface contrast and borders for hierarchy
Use Material Symbols Rounded for all new UI
Do not create custom SVG icons when an equivalent Material Symbol exists
Do not mix Material Symbols with legacy PNG icons on redesigned screens
Custom SVG icons are allowed only when the required product-specific icon does not exist in Material Symbols
The Brain Assistant mascot is an illustration defined by emptyState, not an interface icon
Inactive icons use neutral gray
Active navigation icons use the primary teal accent
The leading icon on a task card is the task type, not media presence.
Do not show the type name as text on the card.
Do not use check or check_circle for TODO; they read as completed.
To do maps from ETaskType.Basic (TASK_TYPE_BASIC). Location is TASK_TYPE_LOCATION and Calendar is TASK_TYPE_CALENDAR. Timer and schedule are not wire values yet.
Use whitespace to separate logical groups
Do not fill empty areas with decorative content. An empty collection may use the emptyState mascot in place of its list or grid
Cards may have different heights when content requires it
Maintain consistent horizontal alignment
Use a status banner for signed-in-not-synced, not a header icon
Warning color is only for the badge, not the whole banner chrome
The banner action must not compete with the floating create button
Media should dominate image and video cards
Metadata should never compete visually with the title
Card actions should remain visually secondary
Do not use colored card backgrounds for ordinary content
The leading icon is the task type from icons.taskType, never a media or content-type icon
Active destination must be immediately recognizable
Use accent color only for the active destination
Do not use filled backgrounds behind navigation items
Keep navigation visually quiet
Use bottom sheets for contextual selection or short secondary flows on mobile.
Do not use a bottom sheet for primary page navigation.
Keep the sheet visually consistent with normal application surfaces.
Use the drag handle only when the sheet can be dismissed by dragging down.
The close action must remain available when dismissing the sheet would otherwise be unclear.
Sheet content may scroll vertically when it exceeds the available height.
Do not introduce decorative shadows, gradients or additional accent colors.
Use existing input, button, chip and typography tokens inside the sheet.
Teal is reserved for selected states and primary actions inside the sheet.
A segmented control is one shared surface, not a row of separate buttons.
For compact selection controls, prefer a subtle selected surface and a thin accent border over a solid primary accent background.
Reserve solid teal fills for primary action buttons and the floating action button.
Selected and unselected segments share one height, icon size and weight.
Inactive segments have no border. Only the selected segment has the accent outline.
Draw one vertical divider between two adjacent unselected segments. Do not draw a divider against the selected outline. Inset the divider from the container's top and bottom edges.
Icons use Material Symbols Rounded at fill 0, weight 400, grade 0 and optical size 24. play_arrow is the exception and uses fill 1.
Do not apply fill 1 to every icon in the control.
Count badges stay visually separate from the label and have no border. Unselected badges use a blue-gray surface. The selected badge uses a teal-tinted fill.
Group the icon, label and count in the center of the segment with a spacing-scale gap. Do not stretch them apart.
Do not use drop shadows, thick borders, or different segment heights.

layout.placement: centered in the free content area

action.omitWhen: the screen already has a floating create action

rules: Show the empty state for the collection that is actually empty. Switching collections changes both the illustration and the copy.
Emptiness follows that collection's count, not a global item total.
The Brain Assistant mascot may look lightly bored, puzzled or waiting. Do not make it distressed.
Mascot illustrations are product SVG assets. They are not Material Symbols and are not recolored to accent.primary.
The mascot fill matches the existing Brain Assistant logo. Props use existing surface, text and icon colors.
Keep the illustration small and leave the surrounding area empty.
Do not add confetti, patterns, gradients or an extra accent color.
Do not add an inline primary button when the screen already has a floating create action.
The title is the accessible name. The illustration is decorative.
Keep the screen header, filters, status banner, floating action and navigation in place.
Teal represents action, selection and success

For compact selection controls, prefer a subtle selected surface and a thin accent border over a solid primary accent background. Reserve solid teal fills for primary action buttons and the floating action button.
Do not use teal simply as decoration
Interactive elements must have clear pressed and disabled states
Dangerous actions must use semantic danger color rather than teal
Do not apply decorative filters to user images
Preserve natural image colors
Do not overlay gradients unless required for text readability
Images should remain the strongest visual element inside media cards
AI functionality should visually belong to the product
Do not use purple AI gradients
Do not use glowing neon effects
Do not use magic stars or sparkles as generic AI indicators
Do not create a separate visual language for AI features
Use normal application components for AI actions and results

avoid: decorative empty-state graphics other than the Brain Assistant mascot defined by emptyState
